items.stem: A sponsor asks the BA to show which requirements are affected if a particular business rule changes. Which BABOK practice most directly supports this?

options.rationale: Correct: traceability links requirements to one another and to designs, so impact of a change can be analyzed.
Onboarding concerns engaging stakeholders, not impact analysis of a change.
Elicitation preparation gathers information; it does not trace change impact.
Grooming orders work but does not establish the traceability needed for impact analysis.

items.explanation: Correct: traceability links requirements to one another and to designs, so impact of a change can be analyzed.

items.stem: Which elicitation technique is most appropriate to quickly gather quantitative input from several hundred geographically dispersed users?

options.rationale: Correct: surveys efficiently collect structured, quantitative input from large dispersed groups.
Interviewing hundreds of users individually is not efficient for this scale.
A single workshop cannot reach several hundred dispersed users.
Document analysis reviews existing records, not new quantitative input from users.

items.explanation: Correct: surveys efficiently collect structured, quantitative input from large dispersed groups.

items.stem: Which TWO elements are typically part of defining a business analysis approach? (Select TWO)

options.text: The level of formality and planned BA deliverables
options.rationale: Correct: formality and deliverables are core choices in the BA approach.

options.text: How requirements will be prioritized and traced
options.rationale: Correct: the approach sets how requirements are prioritized, traced and managed.
Contract pricing is a procurement outcome, not part of the BA approach.
Performance appraisal is unrelated to the BA approach.
Infrastructure selection is not a BA approach element.

items.explanation: Correct: formality and deliverables are core choices in the BA approach.
